When the minimum calculated wall thickness is very close to the standard wall thickness listed in ASME B36.10M, then standard wall thickness will be considered. 6.1.2 Fracture Control The pipelines will be designed to mitigate the risk of running ductile fracture. A ductile fracture mitigation study will be performed during Detailed Design phase to determine minimum required toughness of the line pipe material. The line pipe specification shall include the minimum toughness values for each line size to protect the pipe from running ductile fracture. Crack arrestors may be considered as mitigation to any changes, re‐use of existing off‐spec line pipe, or for select areas identified as necessary where the pipe material does not meet the requirements determined during the final fracture mechanics assessment. 6.1.3 Pipe Coating External coatings will be provided in accordance with 49 CFR 195, Subpart H, Corrosion Control. The exterior of the line pipe will be coated with a single layer of Fusion‐Bonded Epoxy (FBE) 14‐ 16 mils in thickness. An additional layer of Abrasion Resistant Overcoat (ARO) will be applied over the FBE coating for bores and horizontal directional drills. Thickness of the ARO is 30‐40 mils. Field coating application, including girth weld areas, girth weld at directional drill or bore pipe, and coating repairs shall be defined in project specifications to be developed during the Detailed Design phase. Page 10 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 6.1.4 Valves All valves shall meet the minimum requirements of API 6D. Flanges on valves shall be of raised face construction with surface quality and physical dimensions as specified in ASME B16.5 for ASME Class 900 service, suitable for -50OF ambient temperature Mainline valves shall be flanged both ends to facilitate removal and replacement if necessary, during the life of the system. Applications with a need for critical shut‐off will be an plug or ball valves. Currently these locations have been identified by OES as launcher outlet, receiver inlet, and trap bypass valves. Valve actuators will be suitable for the valve types chosen, whether quarter‐turn (e.g., ball valves) or gate valves.
